# The Howling Whispers — Workflow Guide

This file is auto-loaded by opencode. Read it before acting so new chats start with the
deploy pipeline, environment facts, and conventions instead of rediscovering them.

## What this is

The Howling Whispers is a roleplay storytelling web app (React/Next) with four curated characters:
**Coda**, **Heather Whiteclaw**, **Peony**, **Senako Steel**. Stories are generated by NovelAI
(cloud) or Ollama (local/device). The entrance rotates featured portraits including a "Curation
call" ad card linking to the owner's Discord: `https://discord.gg/jrJRrAXBRH`.

## Environments

- **Live**: `https://rp.thehowlingwhispers.com` — public. Service `thehowlingwhispers.service`,
  port 2026, runs from the deployed release worktree.
- **Sandbox/dev**: `https://sandbox.thehowlingwhispers.com` — service
  `thehowlingwhispers-dev.service`, port 2027, `WorkingDirectory=/var/www/HowlingWhispers-dev`,
  `Environment=NODE_ENV=production PORT=2027`, `ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm start -- --hostname 127.0.0.1`.
- **Dev checkout**: `/var/www/HowlingWhispers-dev` (branch `dev`).
- **Main checkout**: `/var/www/HowlingWhispers` (branch `main`).
- **Promote script**: `/usr/local/sbin/howlingwhispers-promote`.
- **Releases**: `/var/www/HowlingWhispers-releases/<sha>` (fresh worktree per deploy),
  symlinked by `/var/www/HowlingWhispers-current`.

## Architecture (post-stabilization)

The app core is intentionally thin. `app/dreambound-app.tsx` is no longer "the entire client app"
— it is the **orchestration core**: top-level state, entrance/login, topbar/navigation, session
orchestration, generation + NovelAI/Ollama + autopilot/impersonation coordination,
storage/persistence glue, and the narrow wiring that composes the feature zones below. Unrelated
feature work must live in its own zone and talk to the core only through narrow interfaces.

> **HARD ARCHITECTURE RULE**
>
> The core was deliberately split out of the former giant `dreambound-app.tsx` because unrelated
> work inside the monolith caused regressions. Do **not** move extracted feature implementations
> back into `app/dreambound-app.tsx`. Before changing something, identify its owning zone; a
> feature should normally be changed inside its own zone and must not duplicate an implementation
> that already lives in the core or in another zone. Do not restructure these boundaries unless
> explicitly requested.

### Ownership zones

| Zone | Path | Owns |
|------|------|------|
| Core orchestration | `app/dreambound-app.tsx` (~5,170 lines) | top-level state, entrance/login, topbar/navigation, session orchestration, generation + NovelAI/Ollama + autopilot/impersonation coordination, storage/persistence glue, feature wiring |
| Character-facing UI | `app/features/characters/character-area.tsx` (~1,089 lines) | gallery, character flow, scene selection, character modals, character-specific UI/helpers |
| Settings UI | `app/features/settings/settings-page.tsx` (~1,108 lines) | settings pane, provider/token management, connection test |
| Chat UI | `features/chat/chat-workspace.tsx` (~1,311 lines) | conversation workspace, message UI, composer, context rail, relationship display, chat-related modals, session persona UI |
| Add-on management | `features/addons/addon-manager.tsx` (~126 lines) | install/enable/export/uninstall add-on packages |
| Changelog UI | `features/changelog/changelog-view.tsx` (~561 lines) | in-app changelog entries (`changelog-entry featured latest` at line 19) |
| Persona / HW-Card | `components/personas/`, `lib/personas/` | persona library, persona editor, HW-Card domain |
| Archive / history | `components/archive/`, `lib/archive/` | story history and archive |
| Generation domain | `lib/generation/` | context compilation, Living Cast, player-turn logic, autonomous cast, starter scenes, story-metadata, howling-addons |
| Character data | `lib/characters/` | canonical representation, Character Card V2, portrait storage, import/export |
| Relationship system | `lib/relationships/` | persistent `(characterId, personaId)` state, events, provider-neutral scorer interface, storage |
| Backups | `lib/backup/` | portable backup payload build/serialize/validate/restore (includes relationship state) |
| World lore | `lib/worlds/builtins/*.ts` | per-character world lorebooks (`coda`, `heather`, `peony`, `senako`) |

## Deploy pipeline (LOCKED — follow exactly)

> **RULE: ALWAYS reboot the site after ANY change to the app (JSX/CSS/route/code), not only after deploys.**
> Run `systemctl restart thehowlingwhispers-dev.service` (sandbox) after every dev change, and let the
> live service be restarted via the promote script. If you skip the restart, the sandbox keeps serving
> a stale asset manifest and the page renders blank/white. Verify with a curl of the page + bundle hash.

1. **Work on `dev` only.** Never touch `main`/live without the user's explicit approval.
2. In `/var/www/HowlingWhispers-dev`:
   - `git pull` (fast-forward `dev` from origin) if not up to date.
   - Make changes, run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.
   - `git add` the intended files, commit with a concise message, `git push origin dev`.
3. In `/var/www/HowlingWhispers` (main checkout):
   - `git fetch origin`
   - `git merge --ff-only origin/dev`
   - `git push origin main`
4. Run `/usr/local/sbin/howlingwhispers-promote` — it builds in a fresh worktree,
   runs tests/lint, does a candidate health check, then atomically switches the symlink
   and restarts via `howlingwhispers-candidate.service`.
5. **After every deploy, restart the sandbox** or it serves a stale asset manifest
   (blank/white page): `systemctl restart thehowlingwhispers-dev.service`.
6. Verify the live release served `(e.g. curl the page and check the bundle hash)`, and
   hard-refresh to avoid stale caching. This was the cause of the earlier "white page".

## Mandatory dev completion workflow

A task is **NOT** complete because `npm run build` succeeded. Build/vite only transpile; they do
not execute the app and will not catch runtime regressions such as a `ReferenceError` during SSR.
After any application/code/CSS/API-route change, the final verification sequence is:

```
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
systemctl restart thehowlingwhispers-dev.service
systemctl is-active thehowlingwhispers-dev.service
```

Then HTTP-check the sandbox and confirm it actually serves successfully (page returns 200 and
contains the app shell / current bundle hash). "Build passed" does **not** mean "deployment
verified."

Use `./scripts/verify-dev.sh` to run the full verify → restart → health-check sequence so the
service restart (and its HTTP check) cannot simply be forgotten.

Do not touch the live service unless explicitly authorized.

## Verification commands (run in /var/www/HowlingWhispers-dev)

- Tests: `npm test` — runs `npm run build` then `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`. **All tests must pass.**
  At the 2026-08-15 architecture checkpoint, the suite contained 225 passing tests; the count only
  grows over time, so do not hardcode an expected total — require "all green".
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- Full workflow: `./scripts/verify-dev.sh`

## Version bump checklist (for a release)

Bump the version in ALL of these together (the version test fails otherwise). The example below
uses the current release family (the codebase is at `0.6.1`; the next release would be `0.7.0`).
Do NOT touch dependency versions like `^0.4.0`:

- `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (`"version": "X.Y.Z"`, both the top-level and the
  `packages[""]` entry).
- `launcher/HowlingWhispersLauncher.cs` (`AssemblyVersion` / `AssemblyFileVersion` → `"X.Y.0.0"`).
- `tests/version.test.mjs` (`assert.equal(packageInfo.version, "X.Y.Z")`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (add a `## X.Y.Z — <name>` section at the top).
- The in-app changelog UI in `features/changelog/changelog-view.tsx` (`changelog-entry featured latest`):
  add a new latest entry and relabel the previous one to its fixed version.

**Standing rule:** every shipped feature batch (user-visible change that reaches `main`)
runs the version bump checklist above and gets a `## X.Y.Z` CHANGELOG.md section. Never
ship user-visible features with a stale version or changelog.

## Content / formatting rules (must be enforced)

- Message/reply format:
  - Spoken dialogue → `"double quotes"`
  - Actions / observable narration → `*single asterisks*`
  - Inner voice → `[square brackets]`
- Action/dialogue/action changes stay inline within the same paragraph; do not automatically insert blank lines when formatting type changes.
- Preserve natural/input paragraph boundaries.
- Adjacent spans of the same type may merge.
- Ambiguous first-person text defaults to dialogue unless there is strong physical/narrative action evidence.
- Already-correct mixed RP remains idempotent.
- The message renderer parses text into inline paragraphs via `buildParagraphs`
  (`app/dreambound-app.tsx:1195`) and must not split on `*…*` or `"…"` into separate block-level
  elements; only actual paragraph breaks (blank lines) create vertical spacing. Keep inline spans
  inside the same paragraph/container.
- Character profiles sent to the model should end with a speech-style paragraph stating the formatting rules. `{{char}}`/`{{user}}` are NOT templated in-app — replace them with the character name / "you" when authoring content.

## Relationship system (V1)

- **Score range**: `-1000` (min) .. `0` (neutral) .. `10000` (max). Asymmetric on purpose: positive
  progression is long, negative decay is fast. Never treated as a percentage internally; the UI
  normalizes via `relationshipMeterPercent`.
- **Identity**: `(characterId, personaId)`. A different player persona has its own relationship
  with the same character. When no persona is selected, a stable default persona is used. Legacy
  `Character.bond` is used only as a migration seed (see `migrateBondToScore`); the `bond` field is
  not destroyed but is not the live state.
- **Scorer**: provider-neutral `RelationshipScorer` interface (`lib/relationships/evaluator.ts`).
  V1 uses a conservative local heuristic; it can be swapped for a dedicated local model later
  without touching storage, events, or UI. It always emits a *delta*, never an absolute score.
- **Where it runs**: client-side in `app/dreambound-app.tsx` (`scoreCharacterReply`,
  `recomputeRelationshipForMessage`) immediately after a character reply is committed.
- **Separation from visible RP**: deltas/reasons are written only to the relationship event store
  (`lib/relationships/storage.ts`, separate `localStorage` key) and to backups — never into
  `Message.meta`, never into the generation prompt. The prompt receives only a non-commanding
  tier/label phrase via the `relationship` context field.
- **Event commit**: `commitEvent` keys each event by a stable `turnId` (`c:<characterMessageId>`).
- **Reroll/regenerate**: same `turnId` → the event is *replaced*, never stacked. **Edit** → remove
  the turn's prior event, re-evaluate, commit. **Delete** → `removeEventsForTurns` for the removed
  character turns. **Rewind/rerun** → remove events for discarded character turns, recompute the
  re-run reply's event. The score is always recomputed from surviving events (`scoreFromEvents`),
  so it stays mathematically consistent with history.
- **Persistence**: `localStorage` ("dreambound_relationships"), restored on load, included in
  backup/export, and re-seeded from legacy `bond` when absent (backward compatible).

## Known issues / constraints (do not silently "fix" without asking)

- Model is slow (gemma-3-12b on CPU on the server). **Do not stress-test.**
- Known regressions the user chose to leave: `finalize-device` drops
  `formatLocalRoleplayReply`; autopilot × JSON structured output overlap.
- Live Coda "we humans" model-adherence issue (Coda is a dog per canon) — known, deferred.
- Live "Check for updates" button deferred by user decision.
- Remote access is HTTP-only and intended for temporary testing (per in-app changelog).

## Connection / Ollama facts

- **This computer** provider: the browser calls the user's own Ollama at
  `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (their Windows machine). Requires
  `OLLAMA_ORIGINS=https://rp.thehowlingwhispers.com,https://sandbox.thehowlingwhispers.com`
  and a full Ollama quit/restart. Verify with
  `curl -H "Origin: https://rp.thehowlingwhispers.com" http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`.
- **Local** provider: Ollama on the website server (CPU-only Netcup), model
  `R4C3R/gemma-3-12b-it-heretic:q4_k_m`, kept hot with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`.
- The connection test (settings) runs as a plain fetch; the user does NOT need to stay on
  the settings screen, but must keep the page/tab open (the panel is inline, not a modal).

## Scene art workflow

- Art assets come from ChatGPT generation and are delivered as Discord attachment links.
- Download the **original** with the signature params from
  `https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...` (media.discordapp.net with `format=webp` is a
  preview; cdn gives the original PNG). Verify 16:9 (typically 1672×941) before committing.
- Save as `public/assets/Heather/heather-whiteclaw-<scene>.png`, then update the scene's
  `background` in `handcraftedScenes` and tune `backgroundFocalPoint`.
- The edit/delete story buttons are for custom scenes only (`scene.id.startsWith("custom-")`);
  curated scenes are locked.
